questions.q: What is a machine element?
questions.a: An individual component or standardised part of a machine that performs a specific mechanical function.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a gear?
questions.a: To transmit rotary motion and torque between shafts with a controlled speed ratio.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of correctly meshing gears over belt drives?
questions.a: They provide positive transmission without slip.

questions.q: What is a pitch circle in a gear?
questions.a: An imaginary reference circle used in gear geometry.

questions.q: Define pitch diameter.
questions.a: The diameter of the pitch circle of a gear.

questions.q: What is the module of a gear?
questions.a: The pitch diameter divided by the number of teeth, m = d/Z.

questions.q: What does Z represent in the gear module relation m = d/Z?
questions.a: The number of teeth on the gear.

questions.q: What is pressure angle in a gear?
questions.a: The angle associated with the common normal at the tooth contact.

questions.q: Name a gear having teeth parallel to the shaft axis.
questions.a: Spur gear.

questions.q: What is the characteristic feature of a helical gear?
questions.a: Its teeth are inclined to the shaft axis.

questions.q: Where are bevel gears commonly used?
questions.a: For power transmission between intersecting shafts.

questions.q: What is a typical application of a worm gear arrangement?
questions.a: Large speed-reduction applications.

questions.q: For an ideal simple gear pair, what relation connects speed and tooth numbers?
questions.a: N₁/N₂ = T₂/T₁.

questions.q: What is a bearing?
questions.a: A machine component that supports a shaft or moving member and reduces friction while allowing controlled relative motion.

questions.q: What are the two broad categories of bearings discussed in the unit?
questions.a: Rolling-contact bearings and sliding/contact or plain bearings.

questions.q: What is the rolling element in a ball bearing?
questions.a: A ball.

questions.q: What is the rolling element in a roller bearing?
questions.a: A roller.

questions.q: What is a plain bearing?
questions.a: A bearing in which motion occurs through sliding contact, often with a lubricating film between surfaces.

questions.q: What is radial load on a bearing?
questions.a: A load acting approximately perpendicular to the shaft axis.

questions.q: What is axial or thrust load?
questions.a: A load acting along the shaft axis.

questions.q: Why is lubrication important in bearings?
questions.a: It helps control friction, heat generation and wear and supports reliable operation.

questions.q: Name one environmental factor that can affect bearing selection.
questions.a: Dust, moisture, temperature or chemicals can affect selection.

questions.q: What is a shaft?
questions.a: A rotating machine member used primarily to transmit torque and power and often to support mounted components.

questions.q: What type of loading is produced in a shaft by transmitted torque?
questions.a: Torsional loading.

questions.q: What commonly causes bending of a shaft?
questions.a: Transverse forces and component weights.

questions.q: State the basic rotational power relation.
questions.a: P = Tω.

questions.q: For speed N in rpm, what is the common power-torque relation?
questions.a: P = 2πNT/60.

questions.q: Name one location on a shaft where stress concentration may occur.
questions.a: A keyway, shoulder or groove.

questions.q: What is a fastener?
questions.a: A component used to join machine components.

questions.q: What component normally works with a bolt to clamp parts?
questions.a: A nut.

questions.q: What is the function of a nut in a threaded joint?
questions.a: It provides the threaded mating element for a bolt or stud.

questions.q: What is a screw generally tightened into?
questions.a: A threaded hole or mating component.

questions.q: What is preload in a threaded joint?
questions.a: The initial clamping force established in the joint during tightening.

questions.q: Why can vibration be important in threaded-joint design?
questions.a: It can promote loosening of the joint.

questions.q: What is a coupling?
questions.a: A machine component that connects two shafts so torque can be transmitted from one shaft to another.

questions.q: What is a rigid coupling intended for?
questions.a: Connecting well-aligned shafts where relative movement is not required.

questions.q: What is the main feature of a flexible coupling?
questions.a: It transmits torque while accommodating limited misalignment and/or damping disturbances.

questions.q: Name one type of shaft misalignment considered in coupling selection.
questions.a: Angular, parallel or axial misalignment.

questions.q: Name two factors considered when selecting a coupling.
questions.a: Transmitted torque/power and speed; shaft size and expected misalignment are also important.

questions.q: What is the first step in machine-component selection?
questions.a: Define the function and operating conditions.

questions.q: Name two operating conditions that should be determined during component selection.
questions.a: Loads and speed; temperature and environment are also important.

questions.q: Why are failure modes considered during component selection?
questions.a: To ensure the selected component can achieve the required reliability and service life.

questions.q: What is quality control?
questions.a: The operational process of checking and controlling production so components meet specified requirements.

questions.q: What is quality assurance?
questions.a: A process-oriented approach concerned with prevention and system-level confidence in quality.

questions.q: What is one important acceptance criterion used in quality control?
questions.a: Engineering drawings, specifications or applicable standards.

questions.q: Why should measuring instruments used for quality control be calibrated?
questions.a: To ensure measurements are reliable and suitable for verifying specified requirements.

questions.q: What should be done after identifying repeated defects in a manufacturing process?
questions.a: Identify root causes, apply corrective action and verify improvement.

questions.q: Why are machine guards used?
questions.a: To protect people from hazards associated with moving machine parts.

questions.q: What does PPE stand for?
questions.a: Personal Protective Equipment.

questions.q: What is the purpose of energy isolation before maintenance?
questions.a: To prevent unexpected release or movement of hazardous energy during maintenance.

questions.q: What should an engineer do when an unsafe condition is identified?
questions.a: Report the defect, near miss or unsafe condition and follow the appropriate safety procedure.

questions.q: Which machine element primarily transmits torque: a shaft or a bearing?
questions.a: A shaft.

questions.q: Which machine element primarily supports a shaft and reduces friction: a shaft or a bearing?
questions.a: A bearing.

questions.q: What is one reason correct machine-component selection improves reliability?
questions.a: It ensures the component is suitable for its loads, speed, environment, life and other operating requirements.

questions.q: What should be considered in addition to strength when selecting a machine component?
questions.a: Stiffness, wear, heat, manufacturability, maintenance, safety, cost and compatibility should also be considered.

questions.q: Why is alignment important in rotating machinery?
questions.a: Poor alignment can increase unwanted loads, vibration and wear and reduce reliability.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a coupling in a power-transmission system?
questions.a: To connect shafts and transmit torque between them.

questions.q: What is the difference between quality control and quality assurance in one phrase?
questions.a: Quality control detects and controls nonconformity; quality assurance focuses on prevention and process/system confidence.

questions.q: What is one major purpose of preventive maintenance?
questions.a: To reduce the likelihood of failure by planned inspection, servicing or replacement before breakdown.

questions.q: In a basic power-transmission chain, what component may connect a power source to a shaft or another shaft?
questions.a: A coupling may be used to connect shafts, depending on the arrangement.
